findings.issue_text: [BUG] useRulerRuleAbility (the singular hook) is called with `rule?: RulerRuleDTO` even though only the plural `useRulerRuleAbilities` was widened to accept `undefined` — the singular hook's signature still requires `RulerRuleDTO`. TypeScript build fails on `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` in the `rule?: RulerRuleDTO` Props type, and at runtime the unchanged singular code path crashes/derives wrong abilities when the list view renders GrafanaPromRuleDTO-only rows where `rule` is undefined.

[BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities calls `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` and `useCanSilenceInFolder(...)` but the diff adds no import or definition for either identifier in this file. Module resolution fails at build time (`useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport is not defined` / `useCanSilenceInFolder is not defined`), so every consumer of useAbilities.ts — including the alert list page — fails to compile.

[BUG] The import of `getRulesSourceName` from '../utils/datasource' is removed, but useAbilities.ts is a large shared file whose other exported hooks (e.g. the prom/cloud ability hooks outside this diff's hunks) previously depended on that import. Build fails with an unresolved-reference error for any remaining `getRulesSourceName` call site in the unchanged portion of useAbilities.ts, breaking the whole alerting package compile.

[BUG] `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` is called with a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO | undefined` in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, but the utility was written for `RulerRuleDTO` (it reads `grafana_alert.annotations`/provenance shape on ruler rules). Type error at compile time (GrafanaPromRuleDTO is not assignable to RulerRuleDTO), and if types are loosened, the provisioned/plugin detection silently returns false for prom-shaped rules, so plugin-provided rules appear editable/duplicable in the new list view.

[ADVISORY] The new skipToken is a module-local `Symbol('ability-skip-token')` used as a sentinel across module boundaries, and RulesTable.test.tsx's blanket `jest.mock('../../hooks/useAbilities')` automock preserves primitive exports but replaces the functions while AlertRuleMenu still compares `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken` against the mocked module's exported symbols. In the mocked test environment, `skipToken` is the automock's copy of the same primitive Symbol value so comparison still works, but any future partial-mock or spy-based mock that re-creates the module loses symbol identity and the skipToken branch silently stops skipping, firing ability queries for every non-Grafana row in tests and masking regressions.

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, but this diff renames/removes the useAllRulerRuleAbilities export (its body is replaced by the new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities in the very next hunk). The file references a symbol that no longer exists, so any consumer of useAllAlertRuleAbilities (all existing CombinedRule-based call sites outside this diff) fails to compile or, if a stale definition lingers, silently computes abilities against the new GrafanaPromRuleDTO code path with a RulerRuleDTO input. No test in the diff exercises useAllAlertRuleAbilities with real hooks to catch this.

[BUG] The federated-rule-group check is replaced with a hardcoded `const isFederated = false;` and a TODO, dropping the isFederatedRuleGroup behavior that previously made federated rules immutable. Federated Mimir rule groups now show Edit/Delete/Duplicate actions they are not permitted to perform; users on the rule list can click Edit on a federated rule and hit a failing save. No test covers federated rules after this change, and the previous behavior's verification was deleted rather than migrated.

[BUG] Removing the ruler query and the ruler-only branch means rules that exist in the Ruler but have not yet propagated to Prometheus render nothing at all, replacing the previous 'Creating' operation list item. A user who just created a Grafana-managed rule sees it silently disappear from the list during the propagation window, with no 'Creating' indicator. The test 'should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists' was deleted instead of migrated, so this dropped requirement has no verification anywhere in the diff.

[BUG] Deleting the promOnlyRules / RuleOperation.Deleting branch means rules deleted from the Ruler but still visible in Prometheus (propagation lag) now render as fully actionable rows via GrafanaRuleListItem instead of a non-actionable 'Deleting' item. Users see and can click Edit/Silence/Duplicate on rules that were just deleted; subsequent operations fail. The 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists' test was deleted rather than rewritten, so the deleting-state requirement is silently dropped with no acceptance criterion covering it.

[BUG] When only promRule is provided (the new GrafanaRuleListItem call site passes no `rule`), useRulerRuleAbility is still invoked with `rule` undefined even though its signature was never widened to accept RulerRuleDTO | undefined (only the plural useRulerRuleAbilities was widened). useRulerRuleAbility(undefined, ...) dereferences the rule inside its unchanged body, crashing the rule list row or returning garbage abilities. Every test in RulesTable.test.tsx fully jest-mocks this hook, so the only-promRule code path — the primary new behavior — has zero unmocked verification; the sibling-hook signature miss is exactly the gap the mocks hide.

[ADVISORY] The rule-view href drops the returnTo query parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader's GrafanaRuleListItem built via createReturnTo(). Users navigating from the rule list into a rule view lose the 'return to list' affordance — after viewing a rule they land on a URL without returnTo, degrading the previous navigation flow with no test asserting href parameters in the new component.

[ADVISORY] The new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities Silence ability replaces the useCanSilence alertmanager-choice logic with [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule], changing the gating model for cloud/external alertmanager setups. Deployments where silencing is served by an external Alertmanager that useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport does not account for will lose the Silence menu item for Grafana rules on the list view; no test in the diff asserts silence ability under a non-default alertmanager choice, so this behavioral redefinition is unverified.

[ADVISORY] canPause/canDelete/etc. are now an OR of ruler-path and prom-path abilities, but no test covers the case where both hooks are live (non-mocked) for the same Grafana rule, including the loading window where the ruler path returns NotSupported and the prom path is still loading. During abilities loading the menu can render Delete/Duplicate enabled and then flip to disabled (or vice versa) as the second query resolves, producing flicker and misclicks on the list view; all RulesTable tests mock both hook families, so this interleaving has no acceptance criterion.

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities, rewired to delegate to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, drops the federated-rule check isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) that the original implementation performed, replacing it with a hardcoded isFederated = false. Federated Grafana-managed rule groups now evaluate immutableRule = false, so the list shows Delete/Edit/Pause actions as supported for rules that are federated and must be immutable — a user clicking Delete gets a failing or wrong-behaving mutation instead of the previously hidden action.

[BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules, discarding the ruler-rule-without-prom-rule branch that rendered newly created rules with a 'Creating' operation state. Immediately after a user creates a Grafana-managed rule, the rule does not appear in its group list until the Prometheus-side propagation completes (and the polling interval elapses), making the rule appear to have failed to save; the deleted test 'should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists' documents the exact behavior this diff removed.

[BUG] The diff deletes the promOnlyRules rendering (RuleOperationListItem with RuleOperation.Deleting) and the matchRules machinery, so rules deleted from the Ruler but not yet propagated out of Prometheus vanish from the list with no deletion feedback. A user who deletes a rule sees it disappear only when the next poll happens, or if propagation is slow they see the rule linger with full Delete/Edit actions re-enabled on it — the deleted test 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists' covered exactly this and was removed rather than ported.

[BUG] The new early-return `if (!identifier) return null` makes RuleActionsButtons render nothing whenever getEditableIdentifier falls through, which happens for any non-Grafana promRule passed without a ruler rule (the RequireAtLeastOne type explicitly permits promRule-only). Any future/current caller that passes only a cloud (Mimir/Cortex) promRule gets an entirely empty action cell plus a logWarning per rule per render — the stated intent was adding promRule support, but the identifier construction under-scopes it to Grafana prom rules only, silently degrading the promRule-only path the new type advertises.

[ADVISORY] AlertRuleMenu now unconditionally invokes both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and ORs the results for every consumer, not just the alert list view the comment scopes the change to. Every existing AlertRuleMenu consumer (rule viewer, RulesTable, cloud-rule contexts) doubles its ability checks and issues Grafana-prom ability requests it never needed before — for non-Grafana prom rules the skipToken guards it, but for all Grafana rules outside the list view the ruler check was already sufficient, so the added requests are scope drift that inflates list-page request count for ~80-rule lists.

[ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the createReturnTo() query parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader version appended to the rule href. Users who navigate from the rule list to a rule view lose the return-to-list navigation context the previous implementation preserved — a behavior change not traceable to the stated 'remove ruler API requests' intent.

[ADVISORY] The component keeps an `operation?: RuleOperation` prop and passes it only to AlertRuleListItem, but after the GrafanaGroupLoader rewrite no call site passes operation, and the entire Creating/Deleting operation pathway the prop existed for is unreachable from the list. Dead public surface on a brand-new component: the next maintainer wiring operation back in has no producer, and the Creating/Deleting UX regression (see GrafanaGroupLoader findings) is masked by the prop suggesting the pathway still exists.

[ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities replaces the silence ability (previously canSilence via useCanSilence on the rule's datasource/alertmanager choice) with folder-scoped permission checks only (silenceSupported && canSilenceInFolder), dropping any alertmanager-choice consideration the old hook performed. Rules rendered via the prom-rule path can show a Silence menu item in contexts where the previous ruler-path logic hid it (e.g. external-alertmanager-only setups), sending users into a silence drawer that may target the wrong alertmanager — a permission-model divergence between the two parallel implementations of the same ability that will drift further.

[BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader dropped the ruler-API fetch and now renders only Prometheus rules, so ruler-only states are unrepresentable. A rule just created via the ruler API (not yet propagated to Prometheus, previously shown with the 'Creating' status via the rulerRule-without-promRule branch) does not appear in the group list at all until the next poll cycle, and a rule deleted from the ruler but not yet propagated (previously the 'Deleting' RuleOperationListItem) now renders as a fully actionable rule with Edit/Delete buttons against a rule that no longer exists. The tests covering exactly these two states were deleted rather than ported.

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities was reimplemented on top of useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` (with only a TODO), dropping the `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` check the old implementation performed. Federated Mimir rule groups, which are supposed to be immutable (no edit/delete/duplicate), now report isFederated=false, so immutableRule is false and users on the rule list/details views see enabled Edit and Delete actions for federated groups — actions the backend will reject or, worse, mutate a rule that federation will overwrite.

[ADVISORY] RuleActionsButtons now calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, ...)` where `rule` is `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` (Props is RequireAtLeastOne and GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule), but the singular hook's signature was not widened in this diff — only the plural useRulerRuleAbilities was. In the new prom-rule-only list path the ruler hook receives undefined; either the call sites don't type-check or the hook's internal ruler-specific handling (useIsRuleEditable with a ruler rule) executes against undefined and returns misleading ability values that then feed the OR with the grafana ability.

[ADVISORY] Every permission is computed as `rulerAllowed OR grafanaAllowed`, a union of two independent permission sources evaluated against the same rule. For Grafana rules rendered from a view that still passes a rulerRule (rule details), both ability stacks run (duplicate permission queries per rule) and the OR means a stale or miskeyed ruler evaluation silently re-enables actions the folder-permission check denies; the two sources have no single owner of truth, so they will drift (the silence logic already diverged between the two hooks in this same diff).

[ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is a near-copy of useAllRulerRuleAbilities with already-diverging logic (canSilence hook vs [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule], ruler-availability gate vs AlwaysSupported). The next ability change (e.g. a new AlertRuleAction or a fix to the immutableRule set) must be applied in two parallel hand-maintained implementations; the silence handling has already diverged in this diff, so the two paths return different answers for the same rule depending on which view renders it.

[ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops `createReturnTo()` from the view URL (`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader applied. Users who click a rule from the list and then navigate back lose the return-to context the old list item provided — the rule view's back navigation no longer returns to the filtered list position they came from.

[BUG] useRulerRuleAbility is called with `rule` that is now optional (`rule?: RulerRuleDTO`) but the singular hook's signature still requires `RulerRuleDTO`, so the prom-rule-only path (the whole point of this refactor) passes `undefined` into a hook that dereferences it. When GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule (rulerRule removed from the list view), useRulerRuleAbility(undefined, groupIdentifier, ...) executes its internal logic against an undefined rule — undefined property access / identifier construction on every Grafana rule row in the new list view, crashing or mis-evaluating the Edit button the diff was built to serve.

[BUG] The rewrite of useAllAlertRuleAbilities into useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with only a TODO, silently deleting the previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` check that made federated rules immutable. Federated rule groups that previously had Edit/Delete/Pause/Restore/RestorePermanently disabled via immutableRule now show as mutable; users in federated Mimir setups get enabled action buttons that fail (or worse, partially succeed) server-side — a behavior regression introduced as an incidental part of a hook refactor, not an accepted requirement change.

[BUG] The rewrite drops the Creating state (ruler-only rules) and Deleting state (prom-only rules) list items entirely, and the corresponding tests ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists', and the matchRules suite) were deleted rather than migrated. During the ruler↔Prometheus propagation window, newly created rules no longer appear in the list at all (they only exist in the ruler API, which is no longer queried) and deleted rules render as normal live rules with full action menus instead of the 'Deleting' operation item — the previous accepted UX contract for propagation states is silently removed, and the test coverage that pinned it was deleted in the same diff so nothing flags it.

[ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the view href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` without the `returnTo` parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx explicitly attached (`createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`). Users who click a rule in the list view and then Edit/back no longer return to their filtered list context; a small UX regression silently dropped during the port rather than an intentional product decision.

[ADVISORY] canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport now OR together the ruler ability and the grafana prom ability, changing the permission semantics from 'the ruler source decides' to 'either source decides' without any stated acceptance of that policy change. A rule where the ruler-based ability check deliberately denies an action (e.g. a provisioned/immutable rule whose ruler check says NotSupported) but where the parallel prom-rule check uses the looser useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities logic will now show the action as available; the menu and the actual action handler can disagree, and users on mixed deployments get buttons the old code intentionally withheld.

[ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities computes `isPluginProvided = isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` where `rule` is a GrafanaPromRuleDTO, but isPluginProvidedRule was written for RulerRuleDTO (the ruler copy passes it a RulerRuleDTO in the same diff), so the check runs against a different DTO shape than it was designed for. If isPluginProvidedRule inspects ruler-specific fields (grafana_alert.pluginData / provenance paths), the check returns false for plugin-provided rules in the new prom-rule-only list view, showing Edit/Delete on rules the old list marked immutable; the two sibling hooks in the same file now disagree on which rules are plugin-provided.

[ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities replaces the alertmanager-aware useCanSilence check with a folder-permission-only check (canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule) for the Silence action. Users who hold folder permissions but lack the alertmanager AlertingSilenceCreate permission (or who use a non-Grafana external Alertmanager) see an enabled Silence menu item whose action then fails or, if the backend trusts the folder check, allows silencing without the silence permission — the previous path (useCanSilence, which consulted the selected alertmanager) enforced this; this must be verified server-side because the hook is client-only.

[ADVISORY] canEditRule and the new OR'd ability checks in AlertRuleMenu/OR-logic (RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx lines 57-67, AlertRuleMenu.tsx lines 70-100) enable an action if either the ruler-derived or the prom-rule-derived ability allows it, trusting the client-side GrafanaPromRuleDTO folderUid for the permission lookup. Because editability is now derived from the promRule's folderUid plus ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata rather than the ruler API's authoritative response, a user who can read the rule list but manipulates which folderUid is associated (or where the prom/ruler data has diverged during deletion) gets a rendered Edit/Delete button; the mutating endpoints must enforce authorization independently — worth confirming no new endpoint trusts these client-derived identifiers.

[ADVISORY] The Cloud-rule RBAC tests mock the plural ability hooks wholesale, so the skipToken path in AlertRuleMenu (passing skipToken to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities for non-Grafana rules and expecting NotSupported) is never exercised by any test in the diff. A regression where skipToken is mishandled (e.g. the hook still issues a folder/RBAC request or returns an ability instead of NotSupported for skipped rules) passes the entire mocked suite; the comment '(useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gets skipToken)' asserts behavior the test never verifies, and users on the list view would get wrong menu actions in production. Checked: RulesTable.test.tsx, GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, RuleDetails.test.tsx are the only test files in the diff, and all of them either mock useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities or grant all permissions.

[ADVISORY] The menu-actions test only asserts the positive case (all permissions granted → silence/duplicate/copy-link/export present) and never denies AlertingSilenceCreate, AlertingRuleCreate, or AlertingRuleRead to assert those menu items are hidden. The new permission gating computed inside useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities — specifically [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule] and the Duplicate/Export rulesPermissions lookups — has no negative coverage; a regression that renders Silence/Duplicate/Export to users lacking those permissions is invisible to the suite. The 'lacks edit permissions' test only covers the Edit button, not the menu items.

[ADVISORY] The new getEditableIdentifier fallback that logs a warning and returns undefined, causing the component to return null, is a new branch with no test in the diff that triggers it. If promRule is a non-Grafana rule and no ruler rule is passed (legal under RequireAtLeastOne), the component silently renders nothing; a regression that instead crashes, or that silently renders buttons, is uncaught. Checked GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx and RulesTable.test.tsx — every render there supplies a valid Grafana promRule, so the null path is never executed.

[ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem component's recording-rule branch and UnknownRuleListItem fallback have no test coverage — every test in the diff feeds it only Grafana alerting rules. Grafana-managed recording rules rendered in the new list view (previously handled via rulerRuleType.grafana.recordingRule in the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader) hit an untested branch; a regression in RecordingRuleListItem props or the prometheusRuleType.grafana.recordingRule predicate ships silently. Checked GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx and FilterView-related tests in the diff — no fixture sets a recording-rule type.

[BUG] The test asserts 'menuItems.length toBe(4)' with the comment 'all 4 menu actions should be available', but the individual assertions only cover silence, copyLink, duplicate, and export — the count is asserted without naming what the 4 items are, so it mirrors whatever AlertRuleMenu currently emits rather than the spec. If a menu item is silently dropped or renamed (e.g. a fifth item like Delete-permanently appears, breaking the count, or Copy Link disappears while the count stays 4 via a different item), the count assertion either fails spuriously or passes without verifying the actual rule-viewer contract — the test verifies the implementation's shape, not the required actions. A spec-required item the implementation omits never fails this test because 4 is read off the current implementation.

[ADVISORY] The RuleDetails test change swaps the cloud rule fixture to a Mimir-backed rulesSource but adds no new assertions, so the diff's claim — that cloud rule details render correctly under the new ability resolution — is still only covered by the pre-existing (unchanged) assertions. If the new ability path in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons breaks the Mimir cloud-rule view (e.g. skipToken mishandling for non-Grafana promRules), the unchanged assertions were written against the old ruler-based rendering and can pass on stale behavior; the fixture change is asserted by nothing new.

[BUG] Removing the ruler API read from GrafanaGroupLoader silently drops every rule that exists in the Ruler but not yet in Prometheus, so just-created rules vanish from the list until Prometheus propagation completes. A user who creates a rule sees it disappear from the rule list during the propagation window (the old code rendered it with RuleOperation.Creating); the same applies to the removed promOnlyRules branch, so rules pending deletion no longer show the Deleting state — users conclude their rule was not created and create duplicates, or re-delete already-deleted rules.

[BUG] The deletion of the promOnlyRules rendering removes the 'Deleting' placeholder for rules removed from the Ruler but still present in Prometheus, so stale rules render as fully live rules with full action menus. Users on the rule list see deleted rules as active and can attempt Edit/Silence/Duplicate against rules whose ruler definition no longer exists, producing 404s from the edit page; previously these rows were clearly marked Deleting with no actions.

[BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the createReturnTo() parameter that the old GrafanaRuleLoader version passed to createRelativeUrl, so the rule href loses the returnTo query param. Users who click a rule name in the list, then click Edit from the rule view, are no longer returned to their filtered list position (pagination/scroll/filter state) — the old href preserved it; this is a regression in navigation fidelity for every list-view click.

[ADVISORY] isProvisioned and isPaused now derive solely from the promRule, and health/error come from rule?.health on a rule that is always defined, leaving dead optional-chaining while summary/state fall back to undefined when the prom rule type is not Alerting — data-fidelity drift from the ruler-driven fields the previous implementation read (annotations.summary, is_paused from grafana_alert). List rows for rules whose Prometheus representation lags or whose annotations live only on the ruler definition show empty summaries; the next change to this component has to reason about which of the two sources of truth each field comes from, and the drift is already observable (summary now comes from promRule.annotations?.summary rather than the ruler's annotations).

[ADVISORY] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated = false where the CombinedRule-based original used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), so the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities shim silently re-enables Delete/Update on federated rule groups it previously disabled. Any caller still on the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities path (Mimir federated groups) gets Delete buttons on rules that cannot actually be deleted server-side — the user hits a 400/403 after clicking; the TODO comment confirms this is a known regression shipped to the deprecated entry point.

[BUG] RuleActionsButtons.V2 calls the singular useRulerRuleAbility(rule, ...) with a possibly-undefined rule, but only the plural useRulerRuleAbilities hook was widened to accept RulerRuleDTO | undefined in this diff — the singular hook still requires a non-optional RulerRuleDTO. GrafanaRuleListItem (new file) renders <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... /> with no rule prop, so the singular useRulerRuleAbility receives undefined on the rule-list view; the hook's internal rule access (e.g. rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) / rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance) dereferences undefined and the action buttons for every Grafana-managed rule crash or fail to render, and the edit/delete buttons silently disappear for users who do have permission.

[BUG] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns { isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading } when folder is falsy, conflating 'still loading' with 'folder lookup failed / invalid UID' — an error from useFolder is silently converted into a permanent deny with no error surfaced. A user with full edit/delete permissions whose folder fetch errors (or whose folderUid is valid but the folder API 404/500s) sees no Edit or Delete buttons and no error message anywhere — the rule list reports the rule as non-editable, silently partial with the API reporting nothing wrong.

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities where isFederated is hardcoded to false (with a TODO), whereas the previous implementation called isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) — the federated-rule immutability guard is silently dropped. Federated rule groups (Mimir feature) that previously rendered as immutable now get editable/deletable ability results: users see Edit/Delete buttons, click them, and the operation then fails server-side — a user-facing action whose guard was removed with no error or indication at the permission-check stage.

[ADVISORY] GrafanaGroupLoader deleted the ruler-group query and the matchRules reconciliation, dropping both the 'Creating' placeholder for ruler-only rules and the 'Deleting' placeholder for prom-only rules, with no replacement feedback. During the Prometheus propagation window, a newly created rule silently vanishes from the list and a just-deleted rule lingers with full action buttons, with no skeleton, status, or warning — users on the list view see work they just performed disappear/appear inconsistently with no error or explanation; the logWarning telemetry for prom/ruler mismatch was also removed so the drift is now unobservable.

[ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities sets MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported whenever loading is false, and its useMemo dependency list omits loading-adjacent values (deps are [rule, loading, isEditable, isRemovable, canSilenceInFolder, exportAllowed, silenceSupported]) while the ability object also depends on isAlertingRule derived from rule — a transient render where rule is defined but folder permissions have not yet resolved yields isEditable false with supported true, showing disabled-but-present actions that flip once data lands, with no loading indicator distinguishing 'checking' from 'denied'. Users with edit permission see the Edit button appear disabled or the menu items render inconsistently during the folder-permission fetch on the rule list page, and cannot distinguish a permission denial from an in-flight check; the list view previously surfaced this via the ruler-availability loading state that was removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useRulerRuleAbility (the singular hook) is called with `rule?: RulerRuleDTO` even though only the plural `useRulerRuleAbilities` was widened to accept `undefined` — the singular hook's signature still requires `RulerRuleDTO`. TypeScript build fails on `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` in the `rule?: RulerRuleDTO` Props type, and at runtime the unchanged singular code path crashes/derives wrong abilities when the list view renders GrafanaPromRuleDTO-only rows where `rule` is undefined.

adjudication.rationale: In `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, the props were changed to allow `rule?: RulerRuleDTO` (via `RequireAtLeastOne<{ rule?: RulerRuleDTO; promRule?: Rule }>`), but the component still unconditionally calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` where `rule` can now be `undefined`. The diff shows only the *plural* `useRulerRuleAbilities` hook was widened to accept `RulerRuleDTO | undefined` (`useAbilities.ts`), while `useRulerRuleAbility` was not updated. This is both a TypeScript type mismatch (passing possibly-undefined to a non-optional parameter) and a runtime risk because `GrafanaRuleListItem` now renders `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule={rule}` (no `rule` prop), making `rule` actually undefined in list view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities calls `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` and `useCanSilenceInFolder(...)` but the diff adds no import or definition for either identifier in this file. Module resolution fails at build time (`useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport is not defined` / `useCanSilenceInFolder is not defined`), so every consumer of useAbilities.ts — including the alert list page — fails to compile.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, the newly added `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` references `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` and `useCanSilenceInFolder(...)`, but in the shown import block there is no import added for either symbol, and the diff does not show any new local definitions for them. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewrite drops the Creating state (ruler-only rules) and Deleting state (prom-only rules) list items entirely, and the corresponding tests ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists', and the matchRules suite) were deleted rather than migrated. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport now OR together the ruler ability and the grafana prom ability, changing the permission semantics from 'the ruler source decides' to 'either source decides' without any stated acceptance of that policy change. A rule where the ruler-based ability check deliberately denies an action (e.g. a provisioned/immutable rule whose ruler check says NotSupported) but where the parallel prom-rule check uses the looser useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities logic will now show the action as available; the menu and the actual action handler can disagree, and users on mixed deployments get buttons the old code intentionally withheld.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably change the UI gating semantics in multiple places from using only the Ruler-based ability to allowing an action if *either* the Ruler ability or the new Grafana Prom ability says supported+allowed. E.g. in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` the `canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport` booleans are now computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)`, and similarly in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` `canEditRule` is OR’d with `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...)`. Whether this is desired is not established by the diff (only a brief comment about list view removing ruler requests). This is a concrete review concern because it can change which actions are shown/hidden when both sources are present and disagree, and the diff doesn’t include an explicit policy decision or tests asserting that “either source decides” is intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities computes `isPluginProvided = isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` where `rule` is a GrafanaPromRuleDTO, but isPluginProvidedRule was written for RulerRuleDTO (the ruler copy passes it a RulerRuleDTO in the same diff), so the check runs against a different DTO shape than it was designed for. If isPluginProvidedRule inspects ruler-specific fields (grafana_alert.pluginData / provenance paths), the check returns false for plugin-provided rules in the new prom-rule-only list view, showing Edit/Delete on rules the old list marked immutable; the two sibling hooks in the same file now disagree on which rules are plugin-provided.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` calling `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` where `rule` is a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO | undefined` (new prom-rule-only path), while the sibling `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` also calls `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` but with a `RulerRuleDTO | undefined`. The implementation/signature of `isPluginProvidedRule` is not shown in the diff, so it cannot be verified whether it safely supports both DTO shapes or inspects ruler-only fields. This is a concrete, diff-grounded risk of inconsistent “immutable/plugin-provided” detection across the two hooks, but the claimed broken behavior (wrongly showing Edit/Delete) is not directly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities replaces the alertmanager-aware useCanSilence check with a folder-permission-only check (canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule) for the Silence action. Users who hold folder permissions but lack the alertmanager AlertingSilenceCreate permission (or who use a non-Grafana external Alertmanager) see an enabled Silence menu item whose action then fails or, if the backend trusts the folder check, allows silencing without the silence permission — the previous path (useCanSilence, which consulted the selected alertmanager) enforced this; this must be verified server-side because the hook is client-only.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes Silence ability computation for GrafanaPromRuleDTO: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` no longer uses `useCanSilence(rule)` (which previously was tied to Alertmanager context/selection) and instead gates Silence with `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` via `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()` + `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)` (see `useAbilities.ts`). This is a concrete behavioral change that could cause UI/ability mismatches in setups where silencing depends on the selected/non-Grafana Alertmanager or non-folder-scoped permissions. However, the diff does not show implementations of `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport`/`useCanSilenceInFolder` or backend enforcement, so the claimed permission bypass/failure cannot be verified as an introduced defect from this diff alone—it's a valid architectural/edge-case concern to review and test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canEditRule and the new OR'd ability checks in AlertRuleMenu/OR-logic (RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx lines 57-67, AlertRuleMenu.tsx lines 70-100) enable an action if either the ruler-derived or the prom-rule-derived ability allows it, trusting the client-side GrafanaPromRuleDTO folderUid for the permission lookup. Because editability is now derived from the promRule's folderUid plus ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata rather than the ruler API's authoritative response, a user who can read the rule list but manipulates which folderUid is associated (or where the prom/ruler data has diverged during deletion) gets a rendered Edit/Delete button; the mutating endpoints must enforce authorization independently — worth confirming no new endpoint trusts these client-derived identifiers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the described OR-logic: AlertRuleMenu now computes canPause/canDelete/etc as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` and RuleActionsButtons.V2 similarly ORs `useRulerRuleAbility` with `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`. The new GrafanaProm ability path (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` -> `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`) bases edit/delete allow on `rule?.folderUid` + `useFolder(folderUID)` + `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(...)` rather than the prior Ruler API-derived editability. However, the finding’s core security claim (that a user can “manipulate” folderUid to gain actual authorization, or that endpoints might trust this client-derived identifier) cannot be verified from this diff because no mutating endpoint authorization behavior is shown—this is a valid, diff-grounded concern to confirm server-side enforcement, but not a demonstrable defect in the PR itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Cloud-rule RBAC tests mock the plural ability hooks wholesale, so the skipToken path in AlertRuleMenu (passing skipToken to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities for non-Grafana rules and expecting NotSupported) is never exercised by any test in the diff. A regression where skipToken is mishandled (e.g. the hook still issues a folder/RBAC request or returns an ability instead of NotSupported for skipped rules) passes the entire mocked suite; the comment '(useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gets skipToken)' asserts behavior the test never verifies, and users on the list view would get wrong menu actions in production. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new skipToken branch for Grafana Prom rule ability checks (e.g., AlertRuleMenu calls useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, ...)). In RulesTable.test.tsx, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is mocked with implementations that ignore the first argument (including the default beforeEach mock: (_rule, actions) => actions.map(() => [false,false])), so the test suite never asserts any skipToken-specific behavior (e.g., that passing skipToken yields NotSupported and does not trigger folder/permission logic). RuleDetails.test.tsx changes the cloud rule source but does not validate skipToken handling either. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The menu-actions test only asserts the positive case (all permissions granted → silence/duplicate/copy-link/export present) and never denies AlertingSilenceCreate, AlertingRuleCreate, or AlertingRuleRead to assert those menu items are hidden. The new permission gating computed inside useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities — specifically [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule] and the Duplicate/Export rulesPermissions lookups — has no negative coverage; a regression that renders Silence/Duplicate/Export to users lacking those permissions is invisible to the suite. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new permission-gating logic for Grafana Prometheus rules in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (e.g., Silence: `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]`, Duplicate/Export via `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`), and updates `AlertRuleMenu`/`RuleActionsButtons.V2` to use `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new getEditableIdentifier fallback that logs a warning and returns undefined, causing the component to return null, is a new branch with no test in the diff that triggers it. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new GrafanaRuleListItem component's recording-rule branch and UnknownRuleListItem fallback have no test coverage — every test in the diff feeds it only Grafana alerting rules. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test asserts 'menuItems.length toBe(4)' with the comment 'all 4 menu actions should be available', but the individual assertions only cover silence, copyLink, duplicate, and export — the count is asserted without naming what the 4 items are, so it mirrors whatever AlertRuleMenu currently emits rather than the spec. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The RuleDetails test change swaps the cloud rule fixture to a Mimir-backed rulesSource but adds no new assertions, so the diff's claim — that cloud rule details render correctly under the new ability resolution — is still only covered by the pre-existing (unchanged) assertions. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the ruler API read from GrafanaGroupLoader silently drops every rule that exists in the Ruler but not yet in Prometheus, so just-created rules vanish from the list until Prometheus propagation completes. A user who creates a rule sees it disappear from the rule list during the propagation window (the old code rendered it with RuleOperation.Creating); the same applies to the removed promOnlyRules branch, so rules pending deletion no longer show the Deleting state — users conclude their rule was not created and create duplicates, or re-delete already-deleted rules.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes all Ruler-side fetching and reconciliation logic from `GrafanaGroupLoader` (deleted `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, deleted `matchRules`, and removed rendering of both the “Creating” case for Ruler-only rules and the `promOnlyRules` “Deleting” case). The new implementation renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` and has no fallback for rules that exist only in Ruler or only in Prometheus. Therefore, during any window where Ruler and Prometheus are not in sync, those rules will be dropped from the list (and no longer show Creating/Deleting states), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The deletion of the promOnlyRules rendering removes the 'Deleting' placeholder for rules removed from the Ruler but still present in Prometheus, so stale rules render as fully live rules with full action menus. Users on the rule list see deleted rules as active and can attempt Edit/Silence/Duplicate against rules whose ruler definition no longer exists, producing 404s from the edit page; previously these rows were clearly marked Deleting with no actions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the entire prom-only handling path in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: it no longer fetches the Ruler group (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` removed) and deletes the `matchRules()` logic plus the `promOnlyRules.map(...)` rendering of `RuleOperationListItem` with `operation={RuleOperation.Deleting}`. Now it renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` as normal `GrafanaRuleListItem`s, which include `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />` in `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`. If Prometheus still returns a rule that has already been removed from Ruler (the exact case previously represented by `promOnlyRules`), that rule will now appear as a live rule with action buttons/menus instead of a Deleting placeholder, matching the finding’s described behavioral regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the createReturnTo() parameter that the old GrafanaRuleLoader version passed to createRelativeUrl, so the rule href loses the returnTo query param. Users who click a rule name in the list, then click Edit from the rule view, are no longer returned to their filtered list position (pagination/scroll/filter state) — the old href preserved it; this is a regression in navigation fidelity for every list-view click.

adjudication.rationale: In the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, `GrafanaRuleListItem` constructed the rule link with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`. In the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, the `href` is `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` passed. This diff verifiably drops the `returnTo` query parameter from list-to-view navigation, which can regress the ability to return to the prior filtered/list state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isProvisioned and isPaused now derive solely from the promRule, and health/error come from rule?.health on a rule that is always defined, leaving dead optional-chaining while summary/state fall back to undefined when the prom rule type is not Alerting — data-fidelity drift from the ruler-driven fields the previous implementation read (annotations.summary, is_paused from grafana_alert). List rows for rules whose Prometheus representation lags or whose annotations live only on the ruler definition show empty summaries; the next change to this component has to reason about which of the two sources of truth each field comes from, and the drift is already observable (summary now comes from promRule.annotations?.summary rather than the ruler's annotations).

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows a deliberate shift in Grafana list rendering from ruler-derived fields to promRule-only fields. The old GrafanaRuleListItem (deleted in GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) derived `summary` from `rulerRule.annotations.summary`, `isPaused` from `rule?.isPaused ?? is_paused`, and provisioned from `rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance`. The new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx derives `summary` from `rule.annotations?.summary`, `isPaused` from `rule?.isPaused` only, and provisioned from `promRule.provenance` (newly added to GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase). Combined with GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx removing all ruler API usage, this creates a concrete data-source drift/regression risk for fields that previously came from the ruler rule. The optional-chaining on `rule?.health`/`rule?.lastError` is indeed redundant since `rule` is required, but that part is a minor style nit; the substantive issue is the changed source of truth for summary/paused/provenance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated = false where the CombinedRule-based original used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), so the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities shim silently re-enables Delete/Update on federated rule groups it previously disabled. Any caller still on the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities path (Mimir federated groups) gets Delete buttons on rules that cannot actually be deleted server-side — the user hits a 400/403 after clicking; the TODO comment confirms this is a known regression shipped to the deprecated entry point.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, the deprecated `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` no longer computes `isFederated` from `rule.group`; it now derives a `groupIdentifierV2` and forwards to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. In the refactored `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, the federated check is explicitly stubbed as `const isFederated = false; // TODO: Add support for federated rules`, whereas the prior CombinedRule-based implementation used `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` to make the rule immutable (disabling Update/Delete). This means federated groups that previously had Update/Delete disabled by the hook will now be treated as non-federated by the deprecated path, potentially re-enabling those actions in the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] RuleActionsButtons.V2 calls the singular useRulerRuleAbility(rule, ...) with a possibly-undefined rule, but only the plural useRulerRuleAbilities hook was widened to accept RulerRuleDTO | undefined in this diff — the singular hook still requires a non-optional RulerRuleDTO. GrafanaRuleListItem (new file) renders <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... /> with no rule prop, so the singular useRulerRuleAbility receives undefined on the rule-list view; the hook's internal rule access (e.g. rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) / rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance) dereferences undefined and the action buttons for every Grafana-managed rule crash or fail to render, and the edit/delete buttons silently disappear for users who do have permission.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims a definite crash because `useRulerRuleAbility` cannot accept `undefined` and dereferences the rule. The diff does not show `useRulerRuleAbility`’s signature/body, so we cannot verify that it still requires a non-optional `RulerRuleDTO` or that it dereferences `rule` unsafely. Moreover, the diff updates `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined, ...)` to explicitly handle `undefined` (guards like `rule ? isProvisionedRule(rule) : false`), which strongly suggests the singular hook can safely flow `undefined` through that path. The asserted “every Grafana-managed rule crash / buttons disappear” behavior is therefore not provable from the diff alone and likely misreads the existing hook’s tolerance for `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns { isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading } when folder is falsy, conflating 'still loading' with 'folder lookup failed / invalid UID' — an error from useFolder is silently converted into a permanent deny with no error surfaced. A user with full edit/delete permissions whose folder fetch errors (or whose folderUid is valid but the folder API 404/500s) sees no Edit or Delete buttons and no error message anywhere — the rule list reports the rule as non-editable, silently partial with the API reporting nothing wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` helper (added in `useAbilities.ts`), when `useFolder(folderUID)` yields a falsy `folder`, the hook returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading }` with no way to distinguish “still loading” from “folder lookup failed / errored / not found” because no error is surfaced/handled in this code path. If `useFolder` can end up with `folder === undefined` and `loading === false` due to an error, the UI will treat the rule as permanently non-editable/removable. However, the diff alone does not show `useFolder`’s error semantics or any UI expectations around error reporting, so this is a concrete edge-case/UX concern grounded in the diff, but not a strictly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities where isFederated is hardcoded to false (with a TODO), whereas the previous implementation called isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) — the federated-rule immutability guard is silently dropped. Federated rule groups (Mimir feature) that previously rendered as immutable now get editable/deletable ability results: users see Edit/Delete buttons, click them, and the operation then fails server-side — a user-facing action whose guard was removed with no error or indication at the permission-check stage.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, the federated-rule immutability check is removed. Previously `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `const isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group);` and included it in `immutableRule`. After the change, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, and inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` the federated flag is hardcoded: `const isFederated = false; // TODO: Add support for federated rules`. This means federated rule groups will no longer be treated as immutable in the ability results, potentially showing Edit/Delete actions that were previously suppressed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GrafanaGroupLoader deleted the ruler-group query and the matchRules reconciliation, dropping both the 'Creating' placeholder for ruler-only rules and the 'Deleting' placeholder for prom-only rules, with no replacement feedback. During the Prometheus propagation window, a newly created rule silently vanishes from the list and a just-deleted rule lingers with full action buttons, with no skeleton, status, or warning — users on the list view see work they just performed disappear/appear inconsistently with no error or explanation; the logWarning telemetry for prom/ruler mismatch was also removed so the drift is now unobservable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the ruler-group query and reconciliation logic in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` is deleted, `matchRules` is deleted, and the UI no longer renders the `RuleOperation.Creating` `GrafanaRuleListItem` branch nor the `RuleOperationListItem` for `promOnlyRules` (deleting state). The `logWarning('Grafana Managed Rules: No matching Prometheus rule found...')` telemetry is also removed along with `matchRules`. However, the finding’s claim about an actual “Prometheus propagation window” causing rules to vanish/lurk cannot be verified from the diff alone (the change appears to assume strong consistency), so this is best classified as a concrete, diff-grounded loss of mismatch handling/observability and potential UX regression rather than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities sets MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported whenever loading is false, and its useMemo dependency list omits loading-adjacent values (deps are [rule, loading, isEditable, isRemovable, canSilenceInFolder, exportAllowed, silenceSupported]) while the ability object also depends on isAlertingRule derived from rule — a transient render where rule is defined but folder permissions have not yet resolved yields isEditable false with supported true, showing disabled-but-present actions that flip once data lands, with no loading indicator distinguishing 'checking' from 'denied'. Users with edit permission see the Edit button appear disabled or the menu items render inconsistently during the folder-permission fetch on the rule list page, and cannot distinguish a permission denial from an in-flight check; the list view previously surfaced this via the ruler-availability loading state that was removed.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the “checking vs denied” distinction is still encoded: `MaybeSupported` is `NotSupported` when `loading` is true (`const MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported;`), so during the folder fetch abilities are marked unsupported rather than “supported but disallowed”. Also, the claim that the memo deps omit `isAlertingRule` is incorrect because `isAlertingRule` is derived solely from `rule`, and `rule` is included in the dependency array (`[rule, loading, isEditable, isRemovable, canSilenceInFolder, exportAllowed, silenceSupported]`). The described transient state (rule defined, permissions unresolved, supported=true leading to disabled-but-present actions) is not directly evidenced by the diff—`useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` propagates `loading` from `useFolder`, which would keep `supported` false until the folder load completes.
